claims.statement: The reviewer and analyzer are two separate deep-agent graphs registered in langgraph.json as `reviewer` (agent.graphs.reviewer:traced_reviewer_agent) and `analyzer` (agent.graphs.analyzer:traced_analyzer).

The reviewer is strictly read-only on the repository: its prompt forbids commits, pushes, and direct gh pr review or review-API calls, and its toolset omits coding, commit, push, and PR-opening tools.

get_reviewer_agent builds the reviewer deep agent per run with reviewer-specific finding, publishing, thread, diff, and read-only helper tools, returning an empty agent when there is no thread_id or the graph is not loaded for execution.
get_reviewer_agent copies the incoming config and configurable mapping before setting its default recursion limit, so it does not mutate the caller's configuration.

The reviewer configures one reviewer subagent for candidate-defect analysis; the parent supplies all finding and publication tools and therefore retains validation, persistence, and publication authority.

PrepareReviewerRunMiddleware performs deterministic pre-model setup: it mints and caches a repo-scoped GitHub App bot token, ensures a replaceable sandbox with that proxy access, and clone-fetches plus checks out the PR head with prepare_review_repo.

Reviewer preparation materializes the applicable unified diff and changed file-side-line set, then passes them as diff_text and diff_line_set in run state so finding anchors can be validated before publication.

Reviewer preparation concurrently gathers PR overview, existing review threads, saved repository style, root and scoped instructions, organization guidelines, and an API-standards skill; it reconciles fetched threads before rendering them into context.

Existing GitHub review-thread comments are wrapped as untrusted XML data; formatter logic validates logins, truncates long bodies, and neutralizes wrapper closing tags so comment text cannot escape its data block.
Findings persist in LangGraph metadata under the canonical reviewer thread rather than the sandbox, so they survive sandbox eviction and are queryable across threads by metadata.kind == reviewer.

A Finding records its location and diff side, severity/confidence/category, content and optional suggestion, status and SHAs, GitHub publication identities, surface state, human-reply and reconciliation fields, diff hunk, fingerprint, and interaction history.
Finding surface states only move forward, so normalization of legacy records reconciles contradictions by taking the furthest-along state.

add_finding resolves diff context from run state, then config, then a fresh authenticated PR diff, and rejects a line range absent from the relevant diff side rather than asking the model to re-anchor.
Each published inline comment embeds an open-swe-review-comment JSON marker keyed by finding ID, which is the exact identity used to associate returned comments and reconcile later review threads.

After a successful publication, publish_review records review and comment identities together, discovers review thread IDs, resolves threads for resolved findings, and advances the reviewer thread's last_reviewed_sha.

publish_review has distinguishable structured outcomes: skipped_empty_re_review with review_id null suppresses a duplicate empty review, dry_run true simulates evaluation publication, and unresolved anchors return unresolvable_findings with remediation guidance.

reconcile_findings_with_review_threads matches findings to GitHub review threads by marker, then stored identities; it backfills publication IDs, marks findings surfaced, resolves a finding only when all matching threads are resolved, and records the latest human reply as needing reassessment.

The reviewer opts into allow_replacement=True because its checkout is reconstructed each run and durable findings outlive the sandbox; if replacement fails, preparation posts a typed on-PR notification and fails the run.
The reviewer starts best-effort diff grouping as a background task for non-reply reviews after diff preparation, so grouping does not block the review.

The analyzer learns a per-repository review-style prompt from historical human PR review feedback and reviewer finding outcomes, using sandbox GitHub access configured with a supplied OAuth token or an App installation token.

analyzer_mode selects bootstrap or continual learning and maps each mode to a bundled SKILL.md playbook; the analyzer's base prompt provides reviewer style themes and points the model to the selected playbook.

Analyzer playbooks are virtual files: launchers seed build_skill_files into the input files channel and get_analyzer mounts a StateBackend at /skills/ in a CompositeBackend, avoiding writes of playbooks to the execution sandbox.

save_review_style_prompt requires repository identity and a nonempty prompt, persists the trimmed prompt with summary, reviewer, and sampling data as completed, and marks the record failed for empty output.
After a successful saved style, ensure_continual_cron idempotently registers one daily analyzer cron per repository, staggered by a SHA-256 hash across 05:00-08:59 UTC, and stores its returned ID.

Continual cron input is threadless but explicitly supplies the repository's deterministic review_style_thread_id and continual mode, preventing get_analyzer from returning an empty agent; absent a supplied user token, preparation resolves an App installation token.

ReviewStyle records are stored in the typed review_styles namespace and track status, prompt and sampling metadata, analyzer thread/run identifiers, cron identifier, error, creator, and timestamps; reviewer prompt lookup fails soft if the store is unavailable.

Bootstrap analysis collects and samples substantive non-bot feedback from recent merged PRs before creating a durable analyzer run, marking the style record failed on collection or run-start failure; immediate continual runs use the same deterministic style thread.
